todos.description: Check the preload behaviour in grid view
todos.context: On branch todo/7-shared-thumbnail-loading, GridViewer.updateItem (internal/gui/ui/gridviewer.go:127-156) now resolves its tile image through the shared resolveThumbnail helper in internal/gui/ui/thumbnail.go and calls gv.schedulePreload() when needsLoad is true, which is meant to reproduce exactly the old condition (the sized Provider.Peek missed). The preload path itself (gridviewer.go:158-199) is guarded by an atomic preloadScheduled CAS, a visibleMin/visibleMax window widened by gridPreloadBuffer (50), a Provider.Gen() generation check and fyne.Do(grid.RefreshItem) callbacks; Provider.Peek/Preload/Thumbnail semantics live in internal/core/imaging/image_provider.go, where peekThumbnail only serves sizes <= maxThumbnailDim (160). The task exists because gridviewer.go has no automated tests, and todo #7 records the risk that a wrong trigger either leaves tiles stuck at embedded EXIF quality or re-arms the preload goroutine from every visible tile.

plan.summary: Todo #8 asks to verify the grid-view preload path that todo #7 touched. The refactor itself is faithful: the old code peeked the sized cache, fell back to the embedded EXIF thumbnail and called schedulePreload on a miss, and resolveThumbnail(size>0) does exactly that (Peek only, needsLoad == Peek miss), so the trigger condition is unchanged. What the reading of gridviewer.go turned up is that the surrounding preload machinery has two real defects and no tests: (a) updateItem records the tile id into visibleMin/visibleMax *after* calling schedulePreload, so the first preload after SetPhotos+ScrollToIndex(500) computes its window from the stale (0,0) range and warms photos 0..50 instead of the ones on screen; (b) the visibleMin/visibleMax bookkeeping uses `visibleMin == visibleMax` as an "unset" sentinel, which is true again after every single-item update, so the range collapses to the last updated tile instead of covering the visible run. On top of that, schedulePreload re-reads thumbPixelSize() inside the goroutine (a resize in between caches images at a size the tile's Peek can never satisfy), a schedule dropped by the preloadScheduled CAS is lost with no re-arm, and the fyne.Do(grid.RefreshItem) callback path is unobservable from a test. The plan makes the provider dependency an interface so the whole path can be exercised, extracts and fixes the visible-range tracking, re-arms dropped schedules, and covers the refresh callback (index mapping + generation guard) with tests; package ui already has widget-level tests (griditem_test.go, thumbnail_test.go) and the Fyne test driver executes fyne.Do inline, so the callbacks are testable synchronously.

steps.title: Give GridViewer a provider interface and cover the preload trigger
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/gridviewer.go replace the concrete `*imaging.Provider` field and the NewGridViewer parameter with an unexported interface (e.g. `gridImageProvider`) embedding the existing `thumbnailSource` from internal/gui/ui/thumbnail.go and adding `Preload(paths []string, size int, onLoaded func(string))`, `Gen() uint64` and `BumpGen()`. `*imaging.Provider` satisfies it implicitly, so internal/gui/app/app.go:125 needs no edit (verify it still builds; the imaging import may become unused in gridviewer.go). Add internal/gui/ui/gridviewer_test.go with a fake provider recording Peek sizes, Preload calls (paths + size) and exposing a channel so the test can wait for the dispatch goroutine. Tests (non-parallel, using test.NewTempApp(t) because build()/Refresh() need a current app): a sized Peek hit shows the cached image and schedules no preload; a Peek miss shows meta.Thumbnail and schedules one preload whose size equals thumbPixelSize() (>= 256, i.e. above imaging.maxThumbnailDim, so the small thumbnail cache is deliberately bypassed); an id past the end of photos/meta is ignored. Drive it through gv.updateItem(id, newGridItem(200)).

steps.title: Extract and fix the visible-range window used for preloading
steps.details: Add internal/gui/ui/gridwindow.go with a small `visibleRange` type (`observe(id int)`, `reset()`, `bounds(count, buffer int) (lo, hi int)`) that starts unset (explicit bool or -1 sentinel, not `min == max`), grows to cover every id observed since the last snapshot, and clamps to [0, count-1]. In gridviewer.go: record the tile id (observe) *before* resolving the thumbnail and calling schedulePreload, so the window that a triggering tile produces contains that tile; have schedulePreload take its bounds and reset the range under the same mutex acquisition, and snapshot gv.thumbPixelSize() there too, passing the captured size into the goroutine instead of re-reading it after a possible resize. SetPhotos calls reset(). Add table-driven tests in internal/gui/ui/gridwindow_test.go for the range type, and extend gridviewer_test.go with: after SetPhotos + updateItem(500) on a 1000-photo list, the preloaded paths are the window around 500 (450..550), not 0..50; a burst of updateItem calls over ids 500..511 yields a window covering 450..561; the window clamps at both list ends.

steps.title: Re-arm a preload request dropped by the preloadScheduled CAS
steps.details: imaging.Provider.Preload only dispatches (internal/core/imaging/image_loader.go Preload returns once every path is claimed or skipped), so the CAS is held briefly - but every tile whose needsLoad lands during that dispatch is silently dropped today, which is the 'tiles stuck at embedded EXIF quality' risk from todo #7. Add a `preloadPending atomic.Bool`: schedulePreload sets it when the CAS fails, and the dispatch goroutine, after Preload returns and before/around clearing preloadScheduled, re-runs schedulePreload once if pending was set (swap it back to false first so the re-run is bounded and cannot spin when nothing is loadable). Keep a one-line comment explaining why the flag exists, since the 'why' is not obvious. Test in gridviewer_test.go with a fake provider that blocks inside Preload until released: updateItem A (blocks), updateItem B with a far id, release, then assert a second Preload happens with a window covering B, and that a single updateItem produces exactly one Preload (no repeated re-arm).

steps.title: Make the loaded-callback refresh observable and test its index mapping and generation guard
steps.details: Add an unexported `refreshItem func(int)` field to GridViewer, set in build() to `gv.grid.RefreshItem`, and have the Preload onLoaded callback call `fyne.Do(func() { gv.refreshItem(idx) })` instead of capturing the grid directly. This is purely a test seam: widget.GridWrap.RefreshItem returns immediately when the widget has no scroller, so an unrendered grid can never show the callback ran. In gridviewer_test.go (Fyne's test driver runs fyne.Do inline, so no extra synchronisation is needed beyond waiting for the dispatch goroutine): a fake provider that invokes onLoaded for a known path refreshes exactly that path's index; an unknown path refreshes nothing; a provider whose Gen() changed between scheduling and the callback (what StopLoading/BumpGen and a folder switch do) refreshes nothing. Also assert StopLoading forwards to BumpGen.

questions.question: Preload window semantics: assume 'accumulate every tile updated since the last dispatch, then reset to the triggering tile' (step 2) unless you prefer keeping today's effective 'last updated tile +/- 50' behaviour - is the accumulate-and-reset version what you want?
gridPreloadBuffer = 50 means up to 101 images decoded at max(tileWidth*2, 256)px per dispatch. Assume the budget stays as is unless you say otherwise (affects step 2 only).

Out of scope unless you say otherwise: changing a colour/favourite filter while grid mode is open never reaches GridViewer.SetPhotos (only enterGridMode in internal/gui/app/navigation.go:110 calls it), so the grid keeps showing the pre-filter list. Should that become its own todo?

OK to widen NewGridViewer's parameter from *imaging.Provider to an unexported interface and to add an unexported refreshItem func field, purely as test seams (steps 1 and 4)? Assume yes; without them the preload path stays untestable.

Should the plan also include a manual smoke check (open a big folder, press L, scroll fast, confirm tiles sharpen and no stall) after the code steps, or is the automated coverage enough? Assume automated coverage plus your own manual pass.

risks: Fyne's test driver executes fyne.Do inline and keeps global app state, so the new gridviewer tests must use test.NewTempApp(t) and must not call t.Parallel(); the project runs tests with -shuffle=on, so any wait on the dispatch goroutine needs a channel or require.Eventually rather than a sleep.

Observing the tile id before scheduling (step 2) changes which photos are warmed first on entering grid mode; this is the intended fix but it does alter cache warm-up order and could surface as different perceived load times.
The re-arm flag (step 3) must be bounded to a single re-run, otherwise a folder where every load fails (Preload's onLoaded never fires on error) could keep re-dispatching.

The stale-index guard still relies on imaging.Provider.Gen(); a photo list swapped without a generation bump would refresh indices from the old list. Harmless today (exitGridMode calls StopLoading -> BumpGen, and LoadFolder clears the loader), but it is the coupling to watch if SetPhotos ever gets called while a preload is in flight.

GridViewer.updateItem runs on the UI goroutine under gv.mu while the dispatch goroutine takes the same mutex; keep the lock scopes as short as they are now, and run go test with -race for these tests.

todos.description: Check what else can be passed to Lightroom
todos.context: The app already hands Lightroom-readable metadata to files: xmp:Rating (5/0 for favorite) rewritten in place inside the JPEG's embedded XMP packet, and stock tags (dc:title, dc:description, dc:subject keywords) written into that same packet and into an XMP sidecar beside the RAW/.ARW pair. Colour labels are the notable gap: model.ColorLabel is red/green/blue only and is persisted solely in the app's per-folder .photo-colors.json, so Lightroom never sees them, while xmp:Label is the natural XMP carrier. The task is a survey: enumerate which fields the app holds today (model.PhotoMeta: Date, Colors, Favorite, Ratable; model.Tags) or could hold, and which of them could be conveyed via the XMP packet/sidecar.

plan.summary: The todo is a survey of what else the app could hand to Lightroom, and the survey's one clear answer is already named in the context: colour labels. Today the app writes xmp:Rating in place inside the JPEG's embedded XMP packet (internal/core/imaging/favorite.go + xmp_packet.go) and dc:title/dc:description/dc:subject into that packet and into the .xmp sidecar beside a RAW pair (internal/core/imaging/exif_write.go, sidecar.go), with an EXIF fallback (ImageDescription/XPTitle/XPKeywords). Everything else the app holds is either read-only from the file (PhotoMeta.Date comes from EXIF DateTimeOriginal or the file creation time and is never written; Ratable is a capability flag, not metadata) or lives only in the app (model.ColorLabel in .photo-colors.json). So the plan is: first record the survey itself (what is written today, what carriers exist, what is deliberately left alone - crs develop settings, GPS, lr:hierarchicalSubject, photoshop:*), then close the single gap it identifies by carrying colour labels as xmp:Label through the same two carriers the rating and the tags already use: read/write inside the JPEG packet in place, and write into the RAW sidecar, wired to the existing colour toggle while .photo-colors.json stays the app's own store.

steps.title: Record the survey of what the app can pass to Lightroom
steps.details: Add a short section to README.md (under Features, next to the Favorites and Color labels bullets) that enumerates, per field: what the app holds and where it is written today - xmp:Rating (5/0, in place in the JPEG's XMP packet, EXIF Rating read as fallback); dc:title + dc:description + dc:subject (packet when it has room, EXIF ImageDescription/XPTitle/XPKeywords otherwise, and the .xmp sidecar for a RAW pair) - and what is held but not passed: model.PhotoMeta.Colors (red/green/blue, .photo-colors.json only; the natural carrier is xmp:Label), PhotoMeta.Date (read from EXIF DateTimeOriginal/DateTimeDigitized/DateTime or the file creation time, never written, so nothing to pass), PhotoMeta.Ratable (a capability of the packet, not metadata). Name explicitly the properties considered and rejected for now, so a later reader does not redo the survey: lr:hierarchicalSubject (Lightroom keyword hierarchy - the app has flat keywords only), photoshop:Headline/Instructions and Iptc4xmpCore:* (no field in the app produces them), xmp:CreateDate/photoshop:DateCreated (would move the photo's date, which the app deliberately preserves), GPS (never held), and crs:* develop settings (present in Lightroom sidecars and must survive every write untouched - see the comment on mergeSidecar). No Go code changes in this step.

steps.title: Give colour labels a Lightroom vocabulary in the model
steps.details: In internal/core/model/color.go add the mapping between model.ColorLabel and the label text Lightroom matches against its label set: a table ColorRed->"Red", ColorGreen->"Green", ColorBlue->"Blue", a LabelFor([]ColorLabel) string that resolves the multi-colour case to a single value by a fixed priority (red, then green, then blue) and returns "" for none, and ColorsForLabel(string) []ColorLabel for the read direction (case-insensitive, unknown text -> nil). Keep it I/O free like the rest of the package. Table-driven tests in internal/core/model/color_test.go covering none, one colour, several colours, unknown label text.

steps.title: Read and write xmp:Label inside the XMP packet
steps.details: Teach the parser and the in-place rewriter about xmp:Label. In internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go: generalise isRatingName into a namespace+local-name check so parseSidecar also collects xmp:Label (field label on sidecarTags, set from the element text and from the attribute form in readAttributes, mirroring setRating). In internal/core/imaging/xmp_packet.go: add packetWithLabel(packet []byte, label string) mirroring packetWithRating - reuse rewritePacket, xmpPrefixes and the element/attribute pattern pair (factor ratingPatterns into a helper parameterised by property name so Label reuses it), and, where the document carries no label at all, append an rdf:Description declaring the xmp namespace exactly as documentWithRatingWritten does. Keep the same read-back check: rewrite, re-parse with parseSidecar, and refuse the write when the parsed value is not the one written. Tests in internal/core/imaging/xmp_packet_test.go: element form, Lightroom's attribute form, xap prefix, no label present (appended), packet with no room (refused), clearing a label back to empty, and that a rating already in the packet is untouched.

steps.title: Expose the label on ExifService: write into the JPEG, report it on read
steps.details: Add internal/core/imaging/label.go with (s *ExifService) SetLabel(jpegPath string, label string) error, built like ToggleFavorite in favorite.go: take the write lock, read the file, find the packet with xmpPacketSpan, call packetWithLabel, patchPacket only when the bytes differ, and return a plain error naming the file when the packet cannot take a label (no packet, read-only trailer, no room, or a form the app does not rewrite) - no whole-file rewrite and no EXIF fallback, so the file keeps its size and layout. In internal/core/imaging/exif_service.go add Label string (and Labelable bool, computed like packetTakesRating) to PhotoInfo and fill both in GetPhotoInfo from the already parsed packet; in internal/core/imaging/image_provider.go carry Label through LoadedMeta so the folder scan can report it. Tests in internal/core/imaging/label_test.go on the JPEG fixtures the favorite tests already use: set, overwrite, clear, and the refusal path; extend exif_service_test.go for the new PhotoInfo fields.

steps.title: Carry the label into the RAW sidecar
steps.details: Extend the sidecar writer so a RAW pair gets the label too. In internal/core/imaging/sidecar.go add the label to what mergeSidecar owns: a strip pattern for xmp:Label in element, self-closing and attribute form (one pattern per property, as the comment on dcElementPatterns requires) and a writer that emits <xmp:Label>text</xmp:Label> inside the same rdf:Description, declaring xmlns:xmp when the element does not already bind it - with the same errForeignDC escape hatch when the prefix means something else there. Choose the API shape: keep WriteSidecar(path, tags) and add WriteSidecarLabel(path, label), so the tags dialog call site in internal/gui/app/tags_action.go is untouched and a colour toggle does not have to know the tags. ReadSidecar keeps returning tags; add ReadSidecarLabel or return the label alongside only if a caller needs it. Tests in internal/core/imaging/sidecar_test.go: new sidecar, sidecar written by Lightroom (crs develop settings and every non-dc property survive byte for byte), existing label replaced, label cleared, foreign xmp prefix.

steps.title: Write the label whenever a colour is toggled
steps.details: Add one core entry point that covers both carriers - e.g. (s *ExifService) SetPhotoLabel(photo model.Photo, colors []model.ColorLabel) error in internal/core/imaging/label.go: resolve the text with model.LabelFor, call SetLabel for a JPEG and WriteSidecarLabel for model.SidecarPath(photo.RAWPath) when photo.HasRAW(), and join the two errors so one failing carrier does not hide the other. Wire it in internal/gui/app/actions.go: handleColorToggle keeps writing .photo-colors.json through colorService (that stays the app's own truth and the source of the filters), then calls SetPhotoLabel on the same goroutine and reports a failure without undoing the JSON write, since the label is an export convenience and the app's own state already changed. Tests in internal/core/imaging/label_test.go for the JPEG-only, RAW-pair and both-fail combinations; the GUI wiring stays a thin call so it needs no test of its own.

questions.question: Should this todo stop after the survey (step 1) and leave xmp:Label to a separate todo? Assume no - the survey names it as the one gap, so steps 2-6 close it - unless told otherwise.

A photo can carry Red+Green at once but xmp:Label is a single string. Assume a fixed priority (red, then green, then blue) picks the one written, rather than a combined "Red, Green" that Lightroom would show as a custom label with no colour - affects step 2.
Label text: assume the English capitalised "Red"/"Green"/"Blue", which matches Lightroom's default label set; any other set name the user configured would show the label as white. Affects step 2.

Should a label found in a file (written in Lightroom) be read back into the app's colour state, or does .photo-colors.json stay the only truth? Assume it stays the only truth: step 4 merely exposes PhotoInfo.Label, nothing reads it into PhotoMeta.Colors.

Should the colour buttons be disabled where the packet cannot take a label, the way the favorite button follows PhotoMeta.Ratable? Assume no - a colour toggle must keep working as a JSON-only label on such files, with the failed file write only reported - affects step 6.

When a JPEG has no writable XMP packet, should the label fall back to the EXIF the way the stock tags do (rewriting the whole file)? Assume no: refuse and report, like the rating path - affects step 4.

risks: Colour toggling is currently a JSON write that touches no photo; after step 6 it patches the JPEG and writes a sidecar, so it becomes slower, can fail per file, and takes the ExifService write lock - a fast run of R/G/B on a big folder now serialises against the folder scan.
xmp:Label appended to a packet with no padding room fails the same way a rating does, so some files will keep a colour the app shows and Lightroom never sees; the error text must say that plainly.

The sidecar merge is regex surgery over documents that carry Lightroom develop settings; a new property pattern that is too greedy can swallow crs:* blocks. The one-pattern-per-property rule in sidecar.go exists for exactly this and must be followed.
Two sources of truth: a label edited in Lightroom and a colour toggled in the app will drift, since nothing reads the label back.

Adding a label field to sidecarTags changes what parseSidecar reports, and that same parser gates the packet writes in appendDescription and documentWithRating - check no existing refusal path changes meaning.

todos.description: Improve keyboard navigation in the Tags dialog
todos.context: In the Tags dialog (internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go) the button row is rebuilt by setGenerating(bool): while a run is in flight it shows Cancel (N) | Background (B) | disabled Generate, idle it shows Close (ESC) | Copy title | Copy keywords | [Save JPEG] | Generate; N and B are not handled by the dialog but by global GLFW scancode shortcuts on the canvas (internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, mapped to OnCancel/OnBlue and dispatched through internal/gui/app/actions.go + tags_action.go, gated by shortcutsBlocked), so they only fire when nothing holds focus and Generating() calls window.Canvas().Unfocus() as a workaround. Escape is already solved separately by the escapeEntry/escapeDateEntry/escapeCheck wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go, which intercept Escape in TypedKey and forward it to TagsDialogCallbacks.OnEscape because a Fyne calendar popup can stack over the dialog; the dialog otherwise relies on default Fyne Tab traversal across Concept, Location, Editorial, Date, claude path, Title, Keywords and the buttons, and this fragile letter-key/focus interaction is what prompted the task.

plan.summary: Move the Tags dialog's keyboard handling into the dialog itself so it no longer depends on canvas-level GLFW scancode shortcuts firing only while nothing holds focus (and on the `window.Canvas().Unfocus()` workaround in `Generating()`). The escape wrappers in internal/gui/ui/escapable.go become a general key router that every focusable widget of the dialog (entries, date entry, check, and a new button wrapper) consults before the embedded widget sees the key; multi-line entries stop swallowing Tab, so Tab traversal actually walks the whole dialog; buttons answer Return as well as Space and, while a run is going, N/B by physical key; and focus is placed deliberately (Concept on open, Cancel while a run goes, a sensible field when the run ends) instead of being cleared. Help text and CLAUDE.md are updated last. The app-side plumbing (actions.go, tags_action.go, shortcuts.go) keeps working unchanged as a fallback for when nothing in the dialog holds focus.

steps.title: Turn the escape wrappers into a key router and let Tab leave the multi-line fields
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/escapable.go replace the `onEscape func()` field of `escapeEntry`, `escapeDateEntry` and `escapeCheck` with `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` calls it first and returns when it reports the key as consumed, otherwise it forwards to the embedded widget. Rename the three types to `dialogEntry`, `dialogDateEntry`, `dialogCheck` (file name stays escapable.go) and rewrite the file header comment: it is no longer only about Escape. Add `func (e *dialogEntry) AcceptsTab() bool { return false }` — the GLFW driver checks `fyne.Tabbable.AcceptsTab()` in `capturesTab` *before* `TypedKey`, so a multi-line `widget.Entry` (Title, Keywords) currently eats Tab and cannot be left by keyboard; overriding it is the only way to make Tab traverse. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` that consumes `fyne.KeyEscape` by calling `d.requestEscape()` and returns false otherwise, and pass `d.handleKey` to every constructor in `buildInputs`/`buildResult`; update the struct field types. In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go update the `[]*escapeEntry` loop in TestTagsDialog_Escape to `[]*dialogEntry` and add cases: Tab is not accepted by title/keywords (`assert.False(t, d.keywords.AcceptsTab())`) and a non-Escape key still reaches the widget (the existing "other keys still reach the input" case covers the latter).

steps.title: Give the dialog buttons keyboard activation and the run's command keys
steps.details: Add a `dialogButton` wrapper to internal/gui/ui/escapable.go embedding `widget.Button` with an `onKey func(*fyne.KeyEvent) bool`: `TypedKey` asks the dialog first, then treats `fyne.KeyReturn`/`fyne.KeyEnter` as a tap (Fyne's Button only answers Space), then falls through to `widget.Button.TypedKey`. Add a helper to internal/gui/ui/shortcuts.go, e.g. `func physicalKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent, key glfw.Key, name fyne.KeyName) bool`, matching `ev.Physical.ScanCode == glfw.GetKeyScancode(key)` or `ev.Name == name` — the scancode form keeps the letters layout-independent like the canvas shortcuts, the name form is the fallback where GLFW is not initialised (it returns -1 then, which would make N and B collide). In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go build every button (`generateBtn`, `copyTitleBtn`, `copyKeywordsBtn`, `saveJPEGBtn`, `closeBtn`, `cancelRunBtn`, `backgroundBtn`) as `*dialogButton`, change `setEnabled(button *widget.Button, ...)` to take `*dialogButton`, and add `func (d *TagsDialog) handleCommandKey(ev *fyne.KeyEvent) bool` = `handleKey` plus, while `d.generating`, N -> `call(d.callbacks.OnCancelRun)` and B -> `call(d.callbacks.OnBackground)`; hand `handleCommandKey` to the buttons and to `dialogCheck` (neither consumes runes, so intercepting bare letters there is safe, unlike in a text entry where the character still arrives through TypedRune). Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: N and B on the focused `cancelRunBtn` reach OnCancelRun/OnBackground only while generating; Return on a focused button taps it; N typed into `d.concept` triggers no callback.

steps.title: Place focus deliberately instead of clearing it
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go add a `shown bool` field set in `Show()` (cleared in `Hide()`) and a small `func (d *TagsDialog) focus(obj fyne.Focusable)` that no-ops unless the dialog is shown — `canvas.Focus` logs "Failed to focus object which is not part of the canvas' content, menu or overlays" for an object in an unshown dialog. `Show()` focuses `d.concept` so the dialog opens ready for typing. `Generating()` drops `d.window.Canvas().Unfocus()` and instead focuses `d.cancelRunBtn` after `setGenerating(true)`, so N/B/Space/Return all act on the run without the unfocus trick; update the comment above it, which explains the workaround. `finishRun()` must move focus off the button that is about to leave the row (the focus manager keeps a pointer to a removed object and keys then go nowhere): focus `d.pathEntry` when `Fail` revealed `pathRow`, `d.title` when tags arrived, else `d.generateBtn`; the simplest shape is for `SetTags`/`Fail` to pass the target into `finishRun`. Tests: after `d.Show()` the canvas focus is the concept entry; after `Generating()` it is `cancelRunBtn`; after `SetTags`/`Fail` it is no longer a button that left `d.buttons.Objects`.

steps.title: Enter in the single-line inputs starts a run
steps.details: In internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog.go extract the Generate button's body into `func (d *TagsDialog) startGenerate()` (guarding `d.generating` and `d.generateBtn.Disabled()`), use it for the button and set it as `OnSubmitted` of `d.concept`, `d.location` and `d.pathEntry` — Fyne fires `OnSubmitted` on Return for single-line entries, so a user can type a concept and press Enter without reaching for the mouse, while Return in the multi-line Title/Keywords keeps inserting a newline. Tests in internal/gui/ui/tags_dialog_test.go: `d.concept.OnSubmitted("x")` (or a Return key event on the entry) runs OnGenerate once and puts the dialog into the generating state; a second submission while generating does nothing.

steps.title: Document the dialog's keys
steps.details: Extend the "Tags dialog" section of `helpRight` in internal/gui/ui/help.go with the keys the dialog now owns: `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` move between fields and buttons, `Space`/`Enter` press the focused button, `Enter` in Concept/Location starts a run, `Esc` closes, and keep `B`/`N` for background/cancel of a running generation. Mirror the same list in the "Keyboard Shortcuts" section of CLAUDE.md (the `B` and `N` bullets currently say "Tags dialog only" without saying that they now work from the dialog itself).

questions.question: Should the dialog focus the Concept field when it opens? It makes typing immediate but means the canvas letter shortcuts no longer reach the app while the dialog is up (they are blocked by shortcutsBlocked anyway). Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 3.
Should Tab move out of the multi-line Title/Keywords fields, giving up the ability to type a literal tab character there? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 1.
Should Enter in Concept/Location/claude-path start a generation? Assume yes unless told otherwise. Affects step 4.

Keep the global fallback (ui/shortcuts.go OnCancel/OnBlue -> app.handleCancel/handleBlue) now that the dialog answers N/B itself, or delete the tags branch of handleBlue? Assume keep — it still fires when a mouse click has left nothing focused. Affects step 2.

Keep the current button order (Close, Copy title, Copy keywords, Save JPEG, Generate), which is also the Tab order, or should Generate come first? Assume keep — the existing test asserts that exact slice. Affects steps 2 and 3.

risks: glfw.GetKeyScancode returns -1 when GLFW is not initialised (unit tests, headless CI), so a scancode-only match would make N and B indistinguishable; the helper must also compare fyne.KeyName.

Bare letters cannot be intercepted inside a text entry: the driver delivers TypedKey and TypedRune separately, so swallowing KeyN in TypedKey would still insert 'n'. Only the buttons and the check may claim letters.
The button row is rebuilt by setGenerating; if focus stays on a button that was removed from the container, the focus manager keeps pointing at it and keys silently go nowhere.
canvas.Focus on a widget whose dialog is not shown logs an error - the focus helper must be a no-op until Show().
Escape from the date entry while the Fyne calendar popup is stacked on top must keep going through OnEscape -> app.handleCancel, which is the only place that can see the foreign overlay.

Existing tests compare d.buttons.Objects by identity and call test.Tap on the buttons; changing the field type to *dialogButton keeps both working only if the wrapper embeds widget.Button and calls ExtendBaseWidget.
